signals.title: NBA President Renews Calls for Press Freedom 40 Years After Dele Giwa's Assassination
signals.summary: [Leadership] The President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Mrs Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya, has renewed calls for press freedom, the protection of journalists and accountability for attacks on media professionals, 40 years after veteran journalist Dele Giwa was killed in a parcel-bomb attack.

signals.title: Afrique du Sud: l’ex-président Mbeki nie avoir «interféré» dans la justice postapartheid
signals.summary: En Afrique du Sud, l’ancien président Thabo Mbeki a témoigné ce 19 octobre 2026 devant la commission d'enquête sur les interférences politiques dans la justice postapartheid, alors que très peu d’anciens bourreaux ont été poursuivis. La commission Khampepe a été mise en place en 2025, après des années de pression de familles de victimes, qui réclament encore justice, plusieurs décennies après la fin de l’apartheid.

signals.title: L’opposant rwandais en exil Robert Kabera retrouvé mort en Ouganda
signals.summary: L’ancien sergent rwandais a été retrouvé décapité près de Kampala. Cet assassinat relance les soupçons sur la traque des opposants à Paul Kagame au-delà des frontières du Rwanda.

signals.title: Senegal debt crisis: Sonko warns G20 plan could backfire
signals.summary: Sonko says the country’s problem is one of cash flow and repayment timing, not necessarily the amount of debt owed. He has warned that the process could reach a political deadlock if the government fails to take what he considers a more practical approach.

signals.title: Centrafrique: cinq acteurs de la journée «ville morte» du 12 octobre auditionnés par la gendarmerie
signals.summary: En République centrafricaine (RCA), cinq leaders de la société civile qui avaient appelé à une journée « ville morte » partiellement suivie le 12 octobre en RCA ont été auditionnés par une unité de la gendarmerie ce 19 octobre. Ils doivent être présentés ce mardi au procureur de la République, qui décidera de leur éventuelle libération ou de leur placement en détention dans une maison d’arrêt. Interpellés le 15 octobre, ils nient avoir sollicité le soutien de l’opposition…

signals.title: Elections 2026 - Meriting Families Demand Electricity After Deadly Illegal Connections
signals.summary: [Health-e] Meriting residents: "lllegal electricity connections claimed 9 lives this year.' Families in Meriting have been waiting for electricity for almost a decade. City Power says electrification depends on municipal planning processes.

signals.title: Massacre de Shakahola : Paul Mackenzie et 28 coaccusés reconnus coupables
signals.summary: Au Kenya, le prédicateur autoproclamé Paul Mackenzie et 28 coaccusés ont été reconnus coupables du meurtre de 191 personnes, dont 190 enfants, dans l’affaire du massacre de la forêt de Shakahola. Le verdict a été rendu lundi par un tribunal de Mombasa.

signals.title: Kenya: Relatives welcome guilty verdict in Shakahola starvation cult massacre
signals.summary: Kenya’s Director of Public Prosecutions, Renson Ingonga, called the convictions a significant achievement, given the number of charges, accused and witnesses.

signals.title: Mozambique: Difficult to control illegal gold mining in Manica – governor
signals.summary:
The governor of the Mozambican province of Manica admitted on Monday, 19 October, that there are difficulties in controlling illegal mining at the “seis carros” mine, where deaths are repeatedly recorded, noting that the site once concentrated around 12,000 artisanal miners. “Many officials went there to visit the ‘seis carros’ mine and see what was…

signals.title: Back to Reality - Masemola Returns As Western Cape Anti-Gang Cop's Home Petrol-Bombed
signals.summary: [Daily Maverick] National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola has returned to work after a scandal. At the same time, an Anti-Gang Unit officer's home was hit in a petrol bomb attack in South Africa's gang-violence capital, the Western Cape, and a suspect died after a related shootout. In another incident in the province, on-duty police officers were injured by people throwing stones.

signals.title: Nairobi Dam Spillway Opened Ahead of El Niño Rains
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Nairobi Rivers Commission has opened the emergency spillway at Nairobi Dam as authorities step up preparations for anticipated El Niño rains and embark on a wider restoration programme for the water body and its surrounding ecosystem.

signals.title: Kenyan Cult Leader, Assistants Guilty On All Charges Over 191 Starvation Deaths
signals.summary: [RFI] A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher and his associates were on Monday found guilty of murdering 191 people, mostly children, in an infamous starvation cult. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the cult base inland from the Kenyan beach resort of Malindi, in what became known as the "Shakahola Forest Massacre".

signals.title: Tchad: l'épidémie de dengue continue de progresser et met en lumière les fragilités du système de santé
signals.summary: Alors que cinq provinces tchadiennes sont désormais officiellement touchées par la maladie qui a déjà fait huit morts pour plus de 3000 cas suspects recensés, celle-ci révèle aussi la faiblesse du nombre de lits de réanimation disponibles dans le pays ainsi que les problèmes d'approvisionnement de ses laboratoires en kits de dépistage.

signals.title: Ouganda: un opposant rwandais retrouvé décapité près de Kampala
signals.summary: La police ougandaise a confirmé, lundi 19 octobre, la mort de Robert Kabera, un ancien militaire et opposant rwandais. Son corps décapité a été retrouvé près de Kampala, durant le week-end. Cet ancien sergent-major et chanteur connu au sein de l'Army Jazz Band – la troupe musicale des forces de défense du Rwanda – était réfugié en Ouganda depuis quelques années. Les circonstances de sa mort et l'état de sa dépouille causent l'effroi et soulèvent de nombreuses…

signals.title: Massacre de Shakaloha au Kenya : Paul Mackenzie jugé coupable du meurtre de 191 personnes
signals.summary: Déjà poursuivi par la justice pour le meurtre d’environ 450 fidèles qu’il aurait poussés au suicide, le gourou autoproclamé a été reconnu coupable d’homicide sur 190 enfants et un adulte.

signals.title: Massacre de Shakahola au Kenya: le gourou d'une secte et ses co-accusés reconnus coupables pour le meurtre de 191 personnes
signals.summary: Le pasteur autoproclamé de l'Église internationale de la Bonne Nouvelle et ses 29 co-accusés ont été reconnus coupables, lundi 19 octobre à Mombasa, du meurtre de 190 enfants et d'un adulte dont les corps avaient été retrouvés dans la forêt de Shakahola, dans l'est du Kenya, en 2023. Paul Mackenzie, qui dirigeait cette secte, prêchait à ses adeptes un jeûne extrême pour rejoindre Jésus. Tous connaîtront leur peine le 6 novembre.

signals.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie faces verdict over 191 starvation deaths
signals.summary: A Mombasa court will deliver a long-awaited verdict on Monday in the trial of a self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher and his associates, accused of murdering 191 people, mostly children, in an infamous starvation cult.

signals.title: Moçambique: Ordem dos Advogados assinala dois anos da morte de Elvino Dias e Paulo Guambe
signals.summary: Em Maputo, há exactamente dois anos, foram assassinados o advogado Elvino Dias e o político Paulo Guambe, na altura membros do partido Podemos de Venâncio Mondlane. Em homenagem, algumas dezenas de advogados voltaram esta segunda-feira 19 de Outubro a juntar-se em Maputo, no local do duplo homicídio, exigindo respostas para o crime que vitimou Elvino Dias, conhecido como “advogado do povo”.

signals.title: Land Disputes, Domestic Violence Linked to Rising Murders in Rwizi Region
signals.summary: [Nile Post] A spate of violent crime in Kazo, Ibanda and Mbarara districts has heightened security concerns across the Rwizi region, with police records indicating that 15 murder cases were reported between September and October, resulting in more than 25 deaths.

signals.title: Mali : HRW dénonce des exactions commises par l'armée et ses adversaires rebelles
signals.summary: L'armée malienne et ses alliés paramilitaires russes ont tué des civils en violation du droit international, tout comme leurs adversaires rebelles, a déclaré lundi Human Rights Watch (HRW).

signals.title: Malian Army and Rebels Committing Abuses Against Civilians, Rights Group Says
signals.summary: [RFI] The Malian army and its Russian paramilitary allies have killed civilians in violation of international law, Human Rights Watch (HRW) has said in a new report, which also confirms the al-Qaeda-linked jihadist group (JNIM) summarily executed Malian soldiers following an attack on a military convoy in July.

signals.title: Security, Traffic Controls Tightened Ahead of Mashujaa Day in Eldoret
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Security has been tightened in Eldoret ahead of Tuesday's Mashujaa Day celebrations, with additional police officers deployed to security hotspots and traffic controls put in place to manage the expected influx of visitors.

signals.title: Resilience Starts At Home - Preparing Communities for El Niño Before Disaster Strikes
signals.summary: [IFRC] In parts of the Karamoja region, north-eastern Uganda, the effects of prolonged drought are already visible. Water sources have dried up or fallen to very low levels. Families are travelling further to find water, while pasture continues to deteriorate, putting pressure on livelihoods that depend on livestock and crop production.

signals.title: Live - Court Delivers Judgment in Shakahola Mass Killings Case
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Mombasa -- Proceedings are underway at the Mombasa High Court as controversial preacher Paul Nthenge Mackenzie and 30 co-accused await judgment in the Shakahola mass killings case, in which they face 191 counts of murder linked to the deaths of children.

signals.title: Kenya cult deaths: Court set to rule in preacher's murder trial
signals.summary: Mackenzie also faces separate charges of manslaughter and terrorism, which he denies. The verdict is being closely watched by victims’ families seeking justice three years after the discovery.

signals.title: Nigeria : le chef d’état-major se rend dans le nord-est après la mort de 15 soldats
signals.summary: Le chef d’état-major de l’armée nigériane s’est rendu auprès des troupes déployées dans le nord-est du pays, quelques jours après une attaque djihadiste qui a coûté la vie à 15 militaires.

signals.title: Kenya : le verdict attendu ce lundi dans le procès du massacre de Shakahola
signals.summary: Au Kenya, un tribunal de Mombasa doit rendre ce lundi son verdict dans le procès de Paul Mackenzie et de 94 coaccusés, poursuivis pour la mort de plus de 530 personnes, en majorité des femmes et des enfants, retrouvés dans des fosses communes dans la forêt de Shakahola en 2023.

signals.title: DR Congo: Ebola outbreak deepens mental health crisis amid stigma and conflict
signals.summary: The World Health Organization has warned that it could surpass the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history, which erupted more than a decade ago and killed more than 11,000 people in West Africa.

signals.title: 13 Dead Following Road Accident in Tete
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- At least 13 people have lost their lives and 20 others were injured following a road accident involving a Yutong passenger bus and a Toyota Hiace minibus in Changara district, in the western Mozambican province of Tete.

signals.title: Mali: HRW confirme l'exécution de soldats maliens par le Jnim et la mort de civils tués par l'armée
signals.summary: Dans un nouveau rapport publié ce lundi 19 octobre, l'organisation de défense des droits humains affirme que le Groupe de soutien à l'islam et aux musulmans (Jnim) lui a confirmé des exécutions sommaires de soldats maliens à Tabrichat, dans la région de Gao, à la suite de l'attaque d'un convoi militaire parti d'Anefis, en juillet dernier. L'ONG Human Rights Watch (HRW) accuse également l'armée malienne et l'Africa Corps russe d'avoir tué et blessé plusieurs dizaines de…

signals.title: Nigeria's Army Chief of Staff visits troops in Borno after deaths of 15 soliders
signals.summary: The Nigerian Army Chief of Staff is visiting troops stationed in the northeast of the country, a few days after jihadists killed fifteen soldiers in the region.

signals.title: Barker Lauds Simba's Firepower
signals.summary: [Daily News] Dar es Salaam -- Simba Head Coach Steve Barker has lauded his side's attacking sharpness after they thrashed Mashujaa 6-1 in a Mainland Premier League match at Uhuru Stadium in Dar es Salaam on Tuesday.

signals.title: Makonda Orders Speed-Up Malya College Expansion Project
signals.summary: [Daily News] Mwanza -- Minister for Information, Culture, Arts and Sports Paul Makonda has ordered contractors to accelerate construction of new infrastructure projects worth 32bn/- at Malya Sports College in Kwimba District. He has set an April deadline for completion.

signals.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case as health officials race to contain outbreak
signals.summary: Kenya has confirmed its third Ebola case, raising concerns over the spread of the deadly virus across East Africa. The Health Ministry says the latest patient is a 65-year-old woman and a close relative of the country’s first two cases. She had been in quarantine since October 6.

signals.title: Chapo Appreciates Work Carried Out By Disaster Risk Management Committees
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has expressed his appreciation for the work carried out by more than 1,500 local disaster risk management committees in disaster prevention and emergency response.

signals.title: Angola Claim Southern African Derby to Start TotalEnergies CAF Futsal Afcon With a Big Win Over Mozambique
signals.summary: [CAF] Angola started their group B campaign with a win at the 2026 TotalEnergies CAF Futsal Africa Cup of Nations after beating Southern African neighbours Mozambique 5-1 on Tuesday at the Complexe Sportif Prince Moulay Abdellah in Rabat.

signals.title: Nduhungirehe, Mali President Discuss Bilateral Relations
signals.summary: [New Times] The Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Olivier Nduhungirehe, on Tuesday, October 13, met with Mali's Transitional President Gen Assimi Goïta for a discussion on bilateral relations, regional security and African integration.

signals.title: Three Dead After Major Fire Destroys a Vessel
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- At least three people have lost their when a passenger vessel burned down while carrying 43 people, including crew members.

signals.title: Three Mozambicans Repatriated After Being Victims of Human Trafficking
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- The Mozambican government has announced the repatriation of three nationals who were victims of human trafficking in the Central African Republic.

signals.title: Chapo Calls for Voluntary Surrender of Illegal Firearms Before December Deadline
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- Mozambican President Daniel Francisco Chapo has warned that the authorities will forcibly collect illegally held firearms after December, when the deadline for their voluntary surrender, under a police amnesty programme, expires.

signals.title: Mourners killed by Kenya police at Odinga national farewell not part of violence, BBC finds
signals.summary: After analysing 1,500 videos and images of the Raila Odinga memorial, Africa Eye finds that those killed were far from the scuffles.

signals.title: Boad Funds 420 Social Housing Units in Ivory Coast
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] The Government of Côte d'Ivoire has officially launched construction work on 420 social and affordable housing units in Yamoussoukro. This project is part of a national emergency program to build 25,000 housing units. The West African Development Bank (BOAD) is providing financial support for this initiative.

signals.title: Ivory Coast Issues a 20-Year Bond, a First for the Region
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] Côte d'Ivoire issued a 20-year Obligation Assimilable du Trésor (OAT) on the West African Monetary Union (UMOA) government securities market. The issuance took place on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. This marks the first time an issuer from the Union has borrowed over such a long term on the regional financial market.

signals.title: Luanda-Lusaka Commercial Flights to Start This Year
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Luanda -- Direct commercial flights connecting Luanda and Lusaka are scheduled to launch later this year, Angolan Minister of Transport Ricardo Viegas D'Abreu announced Tuesday during a visit to the Zambian capital.

signals.title: Malian Army Retakes Strategic City of Kidal After Tuareg Separatists Withdraw
signals.summary: [RFI] The Malian army and its Russian allies entered the strategic northern city of Kidal on Tuesday without resistance after Tuareg separatists announced a tactical withdrawal, five months after government forces were driven out.

signals.title: Afcon 2027 Qualifiers - Coach Aliou Cissé Highlights Confidence Against Malawi
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Luanda -- National coach Aliou Cissé stated, on Monday (05) in Luanda, that the team is confident and will do everything possible to secure the three points, despite acknowledging the difficulties that Malawi may present in Tuesday's match.

signals.title: Afcon 2027 Qualifiers - Angola Tunes Up to Host Malawi
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Luanda -- The national football team trained on Sunday (04) at the 22 de Junho Stadium as part of preparations for Tuesday's match against Malawi, in the second matchday of Group B of the qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).

signals.title: Lone Star's AFCON Road Gets Tougher After Mali Loss
signals.summary: [Liberian Observer] Liberia's long and agonizing wait for a return to the Africa Cup of Nations suffered another painful blow Tuesday night when a late Martial Tia strike condemned the Lone Star to a 1-0 defeat against Mali before a roaring crowd at the Samuel Kanyon Doe Sports Complex.

signals.title: Did Tommy Songo Sustain Injury Before Liberia's Defeat to Mali?
signals.summary: [Liberian Investigator] MONROVIA -- Questions have emerged over whether goalkeeper Tommy Songo sustained an injury after he withdrew from Liberia's starting lineup during the warm-up before Tuesday's 1-0 defeat to Mali in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

signals.title: Egypt, Senegal and Ghana Face Pressure to Relaunch Drive for 2027 Afcon
signals.summary: [RFI] Continental powerhouses Egypt, Ghana and Senegal will attempt to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaigns back on track on Tuesday after opening round setbacks last week.

signals.title: Lone Star Seek to Bounce Back Against Mali in AFCON Qualifying Clash
signals.summary: [Liberian Investigator] Liberia returns home Tuesday to face Mali in a Group K match in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers at the Samuel Kanyon Doe Sports Complex.

signals.title: Morocco, Botswana Discuss Areas for Expanded Bilateral Cooperation
signals.summary: [New Republic] New York -- Morocco's Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccan Expatriates, Nasser Bourita, held talks Tuesday with Botswana's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Phenyo Butale, on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

signals.title: Morocco's Deadly Wall Across Western Sahara - Why the 2,700km Berm Was Built and the Damage It Does
signals.summary: [The Conversation Africa] Western Sahara has been carved in two since the 1980s by a wall that Morocco built to hold on to territory it occupied in 1975. Fifty years on, the conflict remains unresolved and the wall - known as the Berm - remains one of the world's most militarised borders. signals.title: Appel à la grève générale au Sénégal à la veille des premiers JOJ en Afrique
signals.summary: Face au risque de grève générale à Dakar, le gouvernement sénégalais multiplie les appels au dialogue avec le FSDT. L’exécutif cherche à éviter toute perturbation avant le coup d’envoi historique des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse.

signals.title: Kenya : le chef d'une secte reconnu coupable du meurtre de 191 personnes
signals.summary: Le prédicateur autoproclamé Paul Mackenzie et 28 de ses adeptes ont été reconnus coupables du meurtre de 191 personnes, principalement des enfants, par un tribunal de Mombasa, au Kenya.

signals.title: PLU Dismisses Letter Suspending Frank Gashumba As 'Fake'
signals.summary: [Nile Post] A letter purportedly issued by the Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU), announcing the immediate suspension of Frank Gashumba over alleged attacks against Balokole and Pentecostal churches, has been dismissed as fake by the party's General Secretary.

signals.title: Iran foreign minister says Russia, Iran have ‘never’ worked so closely
signals.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Oct 20 that Russia and Iran have “never” worked so closely, as Moscow seeks to play a mediating role in the Middle East war. signals.title: Fire Razes 15 Shops in Oyo
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] At least 15 shops were razed by fire at the popular Bodija foodstuffs market in Ibadan North Local Government Area of Oyo State on Monday, destroying property and valuables worth millions of naira.

signals.title: Lagos - 2 Burnt As Tanker Falls Off Otedola Bridge
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Two people have sustained severe burns after a diesel-laden tanker plunged from Otedola Bridge in Lagos and caught fire beneath the bridge.

signals.title: CAN 2025: le TAS donnera sa décision «fin novembre» sur la finale Maroc-Sénégal
signals.summary: Quasiment un an après la finale de la CAN 2025, le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) annoncera « fin novembre » sa décision sur le recours sénégalais contre la victoire du Maroc sur tapis vert, a indiqué lundi 19 octobre cette juridiction.

signals.title: Two Former Officials Sentenced for the Illegal Killing of a White Rhino
signals.summary: [SAnews.gov.za] The Skukuza Regional Court has sentenced former Kruger National Park Regional Ranger Rodney Landela and former State Veterinary Service Animal Health Technician Kenneth Mochocho for illegal hunting and the killing of a white rhino in a protected area, as well as for possession of a firearm with the intent to commit a crime.

signals.title: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case as regional outbreak spreads
signals.summary: Meanwhile, in the DRC, the outbreak has spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, where two cases, including one death, have been confirmed.

signals.title: RDC : le gouvernement accuse Joseph Kabila de préparer une attaque générale
signals.summary: Vendredi, le gouvernement de la République démocratique Congo a accusé l’ancien président Joseph Kabila de préparer une offensive générale contre le pouvoir de Kinshasa.

signals.title: Ebola en RDC : l'épidémie affecte la santé mentale des populations
signals.summary: Alors que l’épidémie d’Ebola sévit en République démocratique du Congo, les professionnels de santé alertent sur ses conséquences psychologiques. Malades, proches et soignants sont confrontés à une souffrance mentale aggravée par la stigmatisation et le conflit armé dans l’est du pays.

signals.title: Govt Tightens Screening Amid Ebola Outbreak
signals.summary: [Daily News] Dar es Salaam -- THE government has strengthened health screening and surveillance for international travellers entering Tanzania following an Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and a recent case involving a patient who travelled from the country to Kenya.

signals.title: DRC accuses ex-president Kabila of planning 'general attack' on the country
signals.summary: Officials in DR Congo are accusing former president Joseph Kabila of planning a general attack on the country. Kabila on Monday joined forces with the rebel M23 to head a new outfit , taking a more direct role in the insurgency ravaging eastern DRC.

signals.title: Frontline workers in DRC receive Ervebo vaccine amid growing Ebola outbreak
signals.summary: Frontline workers in DR Congo received the Ervebo vaccine on Friday as the country’s worst ever Ebola outbreak continues to spread. Ervebo is effective against the Zaire strain of Ebola. Authorities hope it will offer some protection against the Bundibugyo strain driving the current outbreak.

signals.title: Maroc : 13 anciens ministres reconduits dans le nouveau gouvernement
signals.summary: Ce nouveau gouvernement devra s’attaquer en particulier aux inégalités sociales et territoriales, un enjeu majeur au Maroc

signals.title: Le Kenya renforce les contrôles aux frontières après un deuxième cas d'Ebola
signals.summary: Le Kenya a confirmé un deuxième cas d’Ebola lié à l’épidémie en République démocratique du Congo (RDC). À Busia, à la frontière ougandaise, les autorités intensifient les contrôles sanitaires, tandis que les habitants s’inquiètent des nombreux points de passage clandestins.

signals.title: Chapo Fires Education Minister
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has decided to fire Education Minister Samaria Tovele following controversial and offensive remarks she made toward teachers.

signals.title: Nigeria Prevail but Senegal Draw On Vieira's Debut in 2027 Afcon Qualifiers
signals.summary: [RFI] Powerhouse outfits Nigeria and Morocco launched their campaigns to reach the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations finals with victories over Madagascar and Gabon respectively on Friday night as World Cup participants Senegal and Egypt were held to draws.

signals.title: Afcon 2027 Qualifiers - Vieira Begins Senegal Era As Nigeria Face Early Test Without Osimhen With Groups J-L Getting Under Way
signals.summary: [CAF] Senegal begin a new era under Patrick Vieira, Mali face an early examination against Cape Verde and Nigeria start their TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations PAMOJA 2027 qualifying campaign without injured striker Victor Osimhen as Groups J-L get under way this week.

signals.title: BANA PELE: ECD subsidy expands as government races to close SA’s one-million-child gap
signals.summary: South Africa has expanded access to the early childhood development subsidy to over 954,000 children, but Basic Education Minister Siviwe Gwarube stressed that a large access gap for early learning programmes remained. At the 2026 Bana Pele Leadership Summit, leaders emphasised cross-sector collaboration, policy reforms and private investment to achieve universal access to quality early learning by 2030.

signals.title: Kenya holds back immediate fuel relief as price hikes spark protest threats
signals.summary: Fuel costs are rising just as Kenyan households and businesses struggle with a growing cost-of-living burden. With transport operators threatening fare increases and the government’s price-stabilisation funds under strain, the latest shock could deepen inflationary pressures across the economy.

signals.title: U.S. Raises Kenya Travel Advisory As Ebola Cases Reach Eight
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The United States has raised its travel advisory for Kenya to Level 3, urging Americans to reconsider travel to the country following the confirmation of eight Ebola cases, including one death, amid concerns over regional transmission.

signals.title: Saudi Arabia Targets 108 Cardiac Procedures in Nigeria
signals.summary: [Leadership] The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has launched a medical campaign in Nigeria to provide specialised cardiac care to patients, targeting 108 procedures, including 28 open-heart surgeries and 80 cardiac catheterisation procedures.

signals.title: Mali : Human Rights Watch dénonce des crimes contre les civils [Africanews Today]
signals.summary: Human Rights Watch accuse l'armée, ses alliés russes de l'Africa Corps, mais aussi des groupes armés et jihadistes, d'avoir commis de graves violations du droit international contre des civils. L'ONG appelle à des dispositions urgentes de l'Union africaine.

signals.title: Sénégal: le projet de loi de finances rectificative «pas acceptable» en l’état, juge Ousmane Sonko
signals.summary: Au Sénégal, le président de l’Assemblée nationale et du parti qui y est majoritaire (Pastef) a jugé que le projet de loi de finances rectificative porté par le gouvernement d’Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô n’est « pas acceptable » en l’état. « Pour le moment, nous ne rejetons rien, nous ne validons rien. Mais si c'est maintenu tel quel, nous rejetons », a prévenu Ousmane Sonko, dénonçant notamment la baisse des subventions aux produits pétroliers prévue dans le projet.

signals.title: Au Maroc, la sortie en clair-obscur d’Aziz Akhannouch
signals.summary: Le prochain chapitre du parcours du chef de gouvernement sortant se dessine déjà loin de la politique. Entre confidences de son entourage, retour annoncé aux affaires et ambitions de ceux qui lorgnent son héritage politique, les coulisses d’un retrait.
